FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Third Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by 
the Machine Tools, Machine Tool Elements and Holding Devices Sectional Committee had been approved by the 
Production and General Engineering Division Council. 


This standard was first published in 1964 and revised in 1978 and 1999. The experience gained in implementation 
of the standard has necessitated revision of this standard. In this revision, type C chuck has been incorporated. 
The salient features of Type C taper design chucks body are: 

a) Gripping power increased by nearly 30 percent. 

b) Centrifugal forces are locked. 

c) Entry of chips is restricted, being a better design. 

d) Bearing area of scroll increased by many folds, thus more durable. 

e) Breakage of jaw threads is almost eliminated, being 60° style. 

f) Bigger bores in smaller diameters chucks possible. 

g) Backlash eliminated being spring loaded. 

h) Mounting dimensions as per Type A chucks. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2: 1960 “Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised y. The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 2876 : 2021 


Indian Standard 


3-JAW AND 4-J AW SCROLL MANUALLY OPERATED 
SELF-CENTERING LATHE CHUCKS — SPECIFICATION 


( Third Revision ) 


1SCOPE 


This standard lays down requirements for mounting 
and accuracy of work-holding 3-jaw ad 4-jaw 
scroll operated lathe chucks of normal accuracy for 
general purposes. It covers only manually operated, 
self-centering type of chucks. 


2 REFERENCES 


The following standards contain provisions which 
through reference in this text, constitute provision of 
this standard. At the time of publications, the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are subject to 
revision, and parties to agreements based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of the standards 
indicated below.

(first revision) 

3 TYPES 


3.1 Type A and Type C — Back mounted chucks 
(Chucks which are screwed from the rear). 


3.2 Type B — Front mounted chucks (Chucks which 
are bolted from the front). 


4 TERMINOLOGY 


For the purpose of this standard, the following terms 
shall apply (see Fig.1). 


4.1 Chuck 

Device to be mounted on the spindle nose or a fixture 
of a machine tools for holding a work piece or a tool. 
4.1.1 Manually Operated Self-Centering Chuck 


This type of chuck has a self-centering action and is 
manually operated by means of a key that acts though 
the chuck mechanism to move the jaws simultaneously 
in radial direction. 
4.1.2 Chuck Body 


That part of chuck which carries jaws and encloses 
operating mechanism. 


4.1.2.1 Chuck face 


The face from which the jaws protrude. 


4.1.2.2 Back face 

That faces of the chuck that contacts the face of the 
flange or adaptor when the chuck is mounted on the 
machine. 

4.1.2.3 Bore of chuck 

A through central hole in the chuck body. 


4.2 Jaws 

The work-holding members in chuck which engage 
with the internal mechanism of the chucks and also 
provide the gripping faces. 

4.2.1 Jaw Step Face 

The faces on the jaw steps which are parallel to chuck 
face. 

4.2.2 Internally Stepped Clamping Jaw (Reversed) 
Jaw that the shortest gripping portion towards the axis. 


4.2.3 Externally Stepped Clamping Jaw (Forward) 
Jaw that the longest gripping portion towards the axis. 


4.3 Master Pinion 


That pinion which is nominated as being the one to use 
in order to obtain the most accurate grip. 


IS 2876 : 2021 


JAW STEPPED OUTWARDS _ BODY JAN STEPPED INWARDS(REVERSE JAW) 


Fic. 1 TERMINOLOGY FOR LATHE CHUCKS 


5 MATERIALS 


The various parts of the chucks shall be manufactured 
from the materials as laid down below to meet with the 
requirements: 


a) Body — Cast from a suitable grade of heavy 
duty cast iron having a hardness of 170 HB 
Min or forged or turned from suitable medium 
carbon steel having a minimum tensile strength of 
600 MPa. 


Scroll — Suitable steel of tensile strength not less 
than 600 MPa hardened and tempered 28 HRC 
Min. 


c) Jaws — Suitable steel of tensile strength not less 
than 400 MPa with griping portion hardened and 
tempered to a hardness between 54 to 62 HRC and 
the remaining portion to a hardness of 28 HRC 
Min. 


d) Pinion — Suitable steel of tensile strength not 
less than 600 MPa hardened and tempered to a 
hardness of 42 HRC Min. 


b 


— 


6 DIMENSIONS 


6.1 Dimensions of lathe chucks shall be as given in 
Table 1. 


6.2 Chuck capacities shall be as given in Table 2. 


7 MOUNTING INSTRUCTIONS 


The lathe chuck shall be mounted on the back plate as 
shown in Fig. 2. 


8 DESIGNATIONS 
A chuck shall be designated by: 


a) Numbers of jaws (3- jaw or 4- jaw); 
b) Type; 


c) Nominal size; and 
d) The number of this standard. 
Example: 


A 3- jaw chuck of Type A and of nominal size 160 mm 
shall be designated as: 


Chuck IS 2876 3A 160 
9 TESTS 


9.1 Static Balance 


9.1.1 The static balance of the chuck shall be tested as 
given in 9.1.2. 


9.1.2 The chuck shall be mounted on a mandrel. The 
mandrel shall incorporate an adaptor plate integral 
with it and accurately finished to fit the back plate 
mounting recess of the chuck to be tested The mandrel 
with adaptor plate shall be previously balanced without 
the chuck being mounted on it. The location of the cap 
screws, colts or studs for holding the chucks on the 
adaptor plate shall be in balance. The chuck shall then 
be mounted on the adapter plate and the mandrel placed 
on knife-edges as shown in the Fig. 3 The weights 
required o affect static balance for-centering chucks 
shall conform to the limits specified below.

9.1.3 In all cases, the weights shall be applied at the 
periphery of chuck and the test shall be carried out only 
when the chuck is completely dry inside. 


9.2 Geometrical Test 


9.2.1 Preliminary Remarks 


Since all the geometrical tests to be carried out involve 
the chucks rotation, the chucks should be mounted on 
a test spindled flange or adaptor. This flange or adaptor 
shall have been previously tested for the accuracy of 
size, centering, concentricity with the spindle axis and 
lack of camping of the flange or adaptor. The mounting 
of the chuck on the spindle nose shall be made either 
directly on the face plate or with an adaptor placed 
between the spindle nose and the chuck. In the latter 
case, the above-mentioned tests shall be carried 
out directly on the face plate or adaptor which has 
previously been mounted on the spindle nose. 


9.3 Concentricity of Outside Diameter of Chuck 
The chucks shall meet the requirements as laid down 
in Table 3. 

9.4 Axial Run-out (Camming) of Face of Chuck 


The chucks shall meet the requirements as laid down 
in Table 3.

9.5 Accuracy of Grip on Test Bar 


The chucks shall meet the requirements as laid down 
in Table 4.

9.5.1 The number of test bars to be used is not specified. 
It shall be the subject of an agreement between the 
manufactures and the user. 


9.5.2 The size of test bars to diameters to be used 
shall be proportionate to the scroll pitch so that 
various angular scroll positions differ from one test 
bar to another through an arc subtending an angle of 
approximately 90°. 


9.5.3 In order to ensure the maximum stability of grip 
of the jaw on the test bars, the test bar diameter shall 
never be larger than the internal chuck diameter. 


9.5.4 The contact of each jaw on the test bars shall 
be made gripping along the centre line of each jaw, it 
beings understood that any increase in the number of 
bearings or in their width would upset the centering and 
make the test difficult to carry out. 


9.5.5 Test bars shall be made of heat-treated steel to 
withstand the grip of the jaws without any deformation 
— internal or superficial. 


9.5.6 The accuracy of test bar to be used shall conform 
to the requirements given in IS 2063. 


9.6 Accuracy of Grip on Test Rings 


9.6.1 External Jaws 

The requirements of grip on test rings by external jaws 
shall meet the requirement as laid down in Table 5. 
9.6.2 Internal Jaws 

The requirements of grip test on rings by internal jaws 


shall meet the requirements as laid down in Table 6. 


10 PRESERVATION AND PACKING 


Chucks shall be given a suitable rust prevention 
treatment at the time of dispatch and shall be packed in 
accordance with the best trade practice. 


IS 2876 : 2021 


11 MARKING 


11.1 The chucks shall be marked with the nominal size, 
type and manufacture's name or trade-mark. 


11.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed thereunder, and the products 
may be marked with the Standard Mark.

Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 
“BIS Catalogue” and “Standards: Monthly Additions”.
